title: Customer Insights - Data: MCP server grounds agents in unified customer profiles and insights
summary: Hold: the consent instructions skip selecting the gateway permission, and the controls table presents service-principal creation as equivalent to granting consent. The briefing also understates published Copilot Studio consumption billing and incorrectly treats connector data-policy coverage as undocumented for the Copilot Studio connection.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The tools requiring Customer Insights - Data are read-only.
claims.quote: `create_journey` is the only tool that writes data. It isn't read-only, destructive, or idempotent, so calling it twice creates two journeys. Every other tool only reads.

claims.claim: One MCP server serves both Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys.
claims.quote: One MCP server serves both Customer Insights - Data and Customer Insights - Journeys, but each tool works with a specific app.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The create_journey tool writes Customer Insights - Journeys data.
claims.quote: Validates a complete journey JSON payload, enriches it, validates the enriched payload again, and then creates the Customer Insights - Journeys journey record.

claims.claim: The create_journey tool is not idempotent and retrying can create a duplicate journey.
claims.quote: It isn't idempotent, so retrying a failed call can create a duplicate journey. Have your agent confirm the outcome before it retries.

claims.claim: Profile tools read Dataverse virtual entities reflecting live unified customer data.
claims.quote: They read from Dataverse virtual entities, which reflect the live unified customer data that Customer Insights - Data creates, including its segments, measures, predictions, and clusters.

claims.claim: Get Customer Details returns personal profile attributes and source records identifying which source supplied winning unified values.
claims.quote: Each source record includes the non-system attributes from the source entity, how those attributes map to unified profile attributes, and a flag that identifies which source contributed the winning value for each unified field.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Copilot Studio billing for agents that call this server is not documented and remains entirely a question for Microsoft.
claims.quote: Agents incur charges for generative answer responses unless the agent is created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response doesn't leverage tenant graph grounding.
claims.fix: Separate unpublished server-specific execution pricing from published agent billing. State that Copilot Studio agent usage follows its published Copilot Credits billing and Microsoft 365 Copilot inclusion conditions at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management. For the Microsoft Copilot harness, https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview explicitly includes MCP tools in consumption. Retain only the narrower open question about a separate Customer Insights server charge or feature-specific rate.

claims.claim: The low cost rating means only indirect costs are known, with admin time and an existing Customer Insights licence the only supported costs.
claims.quote: Low. The only cost the sources show is admin time and the existing per-tenant Customer Insights licence; / Copilot Credits are the unit that measures agent usage.
claims.fix: Account for Copilot Studio consumption rather than rating the whole briefing as indirect-cost-only. Set cost to variable for metered agent usage, name Copilot Credits, and explain the published Microsoft 365 Copilot inclusion conditions. Keep separate Customer Insights MCP execution pricing explicitly unknown; do not infer a feature-specific tool-call rate.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; controls[2].ui; controls[2].api; Governance controls table lead
claims.claim: The consent UI and New-MgServicePrincipal are equivalent surfaces for the combined gateway-provisioning and permission-consent control.
claims.quote: Run the commands in this section instead. If you set the server up manually, grant admin consent on your own client app, as described later in this article.
claims.fix: Split the combined row into gateway service-principal provisioning and client-app delegated-permission consent. Keep New-MgServicePrincipal on the provisioning row and the corrected API permissions path on the consent row. State explicitly that creating the gateway service principal does not grant McpServers.D365CustomerInsights.All to a client; do not label the two actions as equivalents.

claims.claim: The maker-side tool selection changes which tools one agent may use, rather than tenant-wide availability.
claims.quote: If you don't want to use all the tools offered by an MCP server, you can selectively turn off MCP server tools directly in your agent.

claims.claim: Tool availability controls select tools, while access to returned customer data remains governed by Dataverse privileges and row-level security.
claims.quote:
Row-level security makes sure users only reach data they're authorized to see
Authorization is enforced inside the tool logic using the caller's user context.

claims.claim: The Customer Insights MCP pages do not give a navigation path for configuring Dataverse security roles or row-level security.
claims.quote: Searched: "Customer Insights" "MCP" "security roles" "configure". Opened the MCP overview, full tools reference and gateway connection page. They require and discuss Dataverse privileges but give no security-role configuration path; surrounding Dataverse role guidance exists.

claims.claim: A data policy regulating Power Platform connectors also regulates access to MCP servers and their tools in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Access to MCP servers in Copilot Studio relies on Power Platform connectors for connectivity. This condition means that if a data policy regulates Power Platform connectors, it also regulates access to the MCP server and its tools for your agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that Power Platform data policies apply when Customer Insights is connected to a Copilot Studio agent through the gateway.
claims.quote: The process is the same, whether you're adding prebuilt Microsoft MCP connectors or an MCP server to which you configured a connection.
claims.fix: Remove the unsupported exception for the Copilot Studio gateway connection. State that the cited Copilot Studio MCP documentation applies connector data policies to both prebuilt and configured MCP connections, which includes the documented Customer Insights Copilot Studio connection. Do not extend that coverage to external MCP clients; any remaining open question should be confined to those clients or to a particular policy configuration.
